title: V2X reception: awareness ratio, PDR-vs-distance shape, effective range, latency
scope: Communication panel. Awareness/PDR curves are reconstructed from MA reports joined to ground-truth emission positions, so they are proportional-to-PDR curves normalised at the near band, not absolute PDR.
curated_from: docs/realism/investigation/research-realism-benchmarks.json (benchmarks[10,11,12,14], findings section B), docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json (findings section 4, measurement campaigns usable as calibration references), and docs/realism/ROADMAP.md sections 4 (Phase 2 gate) and 5.

awareness_ratio_200m_urban_min.cite: ROADMAP Phase-2 gate (Boban & d'Orey measurement campaign)
awareness_ratio_200m_urban_min.source: Project-adopted gate from docs/realism/ROADMAP.md section 5 comm panel and the Phase-2 benchmark gate: '>= 90% neighbor-awareness at 200 m urban ... under low load (reference: Boban & d'Orey 2015 measurement campaign)'. The underlying campaign is Boban & d'Orey, 'Exploring the Practical Limits of Cooperative Awareness in Vehicular Communications', https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06590 (measurements at 4 EU sites plus large-scale GEMV2 simulation), which reports 90% awareness achievable up to ~200 m urban. Neighbour-awareness ratio is defined as detected neighbours / neighbours physically present within a nominal range inside a freshness window -- EURECOM, 'Rethinking Cooperative Awareness for Future V2X Safety-critical Applications', https://www.eurecom.fr/publication/5365/download/comsys-publi-5365.pdf.
awareness_ratio_200m_urban_min.note: RETIRED AS A GATE 2026-09-01 -- DO NOT RE-ATTACH IT TO AN ALL-PAIRS PER-PACKET RATIO. The full paper was read and its conditions are transcribed in v2x_awareness_conditions (same directory); four of them differ from any harness metric that reads a normalised awareness ratio at a fixed 200 m. (1) POPULATION: the measured '200 m urban' is ONE cell of Table III -- Tampere, a THREE-vehicle instrumented fleet on a shared 22 km route, where the denominator counts only instrumented vehicles. (2) SHOT MULTIPLICITY: NAR is a '>= 1 message in t = 1 s' metric at 10 Hz CAM, modelled as 1 - (1 - PDR)^Z with Z fitted 2.1365-8.2886, so NAR 0.90 is a PER-PACKET PDR of 0.344 at the urban Z = 5.4579, not 0.90; a 1 Hz engine has Z = 1 and reports per-packet PDR directly. (3) LINK BUDGET: the comparable simulated arm assumed a -95 dBm receiver, so its 200 m point sits at 110 dB against the harness's 104 dB (23 dBm into -81 dBm). (4) LEVEL vs CROSSING: Table III reports the DISTANCE at which NAR falls below 0.90, not a value at 200 m. The like-for-like restatement is comm.nar90_equivalent_range_m (src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/awareness.py); see docs/realism/AWARENESS-GATE.md. This entry stays pinned because the NUMBER is real and correctly cited -- what was wrong was the comparison. Original note, still true: see pathloss_37885.nlos_link_budget_consequence_m -- at 200 m an urban NLOS link needs ~39 dBm to close, so this figure is in practice a statement about the LOS/NLOSv share of the scenario's links, which is now measured directly as comm.link_state_los_fraction_200m (0.060 on real Ingolstadt geometry).

awareness_ratio_500m_highway_min.cite: ROADMAP Phase-2 gate (Boban & d'Orey measurement campaign)
awareness_ratio_500m_highway_min.source: Same source and caveat as awareness_ratio_200m_urban_min: docs/realism/ROADMAP.md Phase-2 gate, '>= 90% neighbor-awareness ... at 500 m highway under low load', matching Boban & d'Orey's reported '>500 m highway' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06590, summarised in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json findings section 4).
awareness_ratio_500m_highway_min.note: OVERSTATED BY ITS SOURCE, recorded 2026-09-01 after reading the full paper: '>500 m highway' appears only in the ABSTRACT. Table III's largest MEASURED highway V2V figure is 400 m (Finland; the other three sites give 100, 250 and 200 m), and the largest SIMULATED one is also 400 m, at 20 dBm into a -95 dBm receiver (Section V-E.2). Nothing in the body supports 500 m. Treat this entry as a project aspiration, not a transcription; the audited highway point is v2x_awareness_conditions.simulated_highway_nar90. Not evaluated by the Phase-0 anchors (100/200/300 m); pinned so Phase 2 uses the same audited number. LINK-BUDGET CHECK: TR 37.885 highway LOS at 500 m is 101.7964 dB (pathloss_37885.pathloss_at_reference_distances_db), so with the vendored -81 dBm sensitivity this gate needs >= 20.8 dBm EIRP -- the vendored VeReMi-NextGen 0.02 W (13.01 dBm) transmit power reaches only ~204 m and CANNOT satisfy it. Phase 2 must raise transmit power (typical DSRC OBU 20-23 dBm) before this gate is meaningful.

awareness_anchor_distances_m.source: docs/realism/investigation/research-realism-benchmarks.json benchmarks[14] (awareness metrics: neighbor awareness ratio, EURECOM 'Rethinking Cooperative Awareness'): 'Track NAR at 100/200/300 m vs density'; adopted verbatim in docs/realism/ROADMAP.md Phase 0 task list.
awareness_anchor_distances_m.note: The three distances at which the normalised awareness ratio is reported.

awareness_limiting_factor.source: Boban & d'Orey, 'Exploring the Practical Limits of Cooperative Awareness in Vehicular Communications' (https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06590): cooperative-awareness delivery is dominated by SHADOWING rather than by channel load at the beaconing rates studied -- increasing transmit power improves awareness more than increasing beacon rate does. Recorded in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json findings section 4 as 'delivery dominated by shadowing (power beats rate)'.
awareness_limiting_factor.note: MODEL CONSEQUENCE, pinned as a falsifiable expectation for Phase 2: under the geometric radio model, sweeping transmit power must move the awareness curve MORE than sweeping the beacon rate does at low-to-moderate density. If the implemented model shows the opposite ordering, the congestion/CBR term is overweighted relative to the propagation term.

pdr_gray_zone_width_min_m.source: Project-adopted gate from docs/realism/ROADMAP.md section 5: 'PDR gray-zone width (90% -> 20%) >= 100 m', referencing the DSRC empirical characterisation of Bai, Stancil & Krishnan, 'Toward understanding characteristics of dedicated short range communications (DSRC) from a perspective of vehicular network engineers', ACM MobiCom 2010, doi:10.1145/1859995.1860033, which establishes the three-zone shape: a near-deterministic reliable zone, a wide stochastic gray zone in which PDR falls gradually, and a far zone of near-zero delivery.
pdr_gray_zone_width_min_m.derivation: RATIONALE for the >= 100 m figure, made quantitative: with a hard receive threshold and log-normal shadowing of standard deviation sigma, PDR(d) = Phi(margin(d)/sigma), so moving from PDR 0.90 to 0.20 costs a fixed 2.1232*sigma dB of margin (Phi^-1(0.9) - Phi^-1(0.2) = 1.281552 + 0.841621). Dividing by the path-loss slope b gives a pure distance RATIO d20/d90 = 10^(2.1232*sigma/b): 2.4066 for urban LOS (sigma 3.0, b 16.7), 2.0820 for highway LOS (sigma 3.0, b 20), 1.9191 for urban NLOS (sigma 4.0, b 30). See gray_zone_ratio_from_shadowing for the pinned values.
pdr_gray_zone_width_min_m.note: A step-function (unit-disc) range model FAILS this by construction -- that is the intended Phase-0 baseline finding, not a harness defect. Because the width is a fixed MULTIPLE of d90, the gate is only reachable once d90 is large enough: >= 71 m urban LOS, >= 92 m highway LOS, >= 109 m urban NLOS. Small-scale fading widens the zone further, so these are floors.

gray_zone_ratio_from_shadowing.unit: [state, shadowing sigma dB, path-loss slope b, d20/d90 ratio, minimum d90 in m for a 100 m gray zone]
gray_zone_ratio_from_shadowing.cite: derived: log-normal shadowing through the TR 37.885 slopes
gray_zone_ratio_from_shadowing.source: Derived on 2026-08-30 from the anchored TR 37.885 slopes (pathloss_37885.urban_los / highway_los / urban_nlos) and shadowing sigmas (pathloss_37885.shadowing_sigma_db) under a hard receive-threshold model: d20/d90 = 10^((Phi^-1(0.9) - Phi^-1(0.2)) * sigma / b), and the last column is 100 / (ratio - 1), the smallest 90%-crossing distance at which the gate pdr_gray_zone_width_min_m can be met by shadowing alone.
gray_zone_ratio_from_shadowing.derivation: Phi^-1(0.9) - Phi^-1(0.2) = 2.123173 (computed with statistics.NormalDist, double precision); shadowing-only, no small-scale fading, no NLOS/LOS state mixing, no MAC losses -- every one of those widens the zone further, so these ratios are LOWER BOUNDS.
gray_zone_ratio_from_shadowing.note: DIAGNOSTIC, not a gate. If the Phase-2 comm panel reports a gray-zone ratio materially BELOW these values, the shadowing process is being applied with too small a sigma or is being re-drawn per packet (which averages the zone away); materially above, the link population is mixing propagation states or the fading term dominates.

effective_range_pdr_min.cite: Safety Pilot Model Deployment (Ann Arbor) 'effective range' definition
effective_range_pdr_min.source: The Safety Pilot Model Deployment DSRC field study defines EFFECTIVE RANGE as the distance at which packet delivery ratio falls to 50%: 'Empirical Study of DSRC Performance Based on Safety Pilot Model Deployment Data', IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08365 (world's largest connected-vehicle deployment; also quantifies PDR degradation from foliage, weather, buildings, travel direction and road elevation). Recorded in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json findings section 4 and required by docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md 'Reference curves to pin as refdata'.
effective_range_pdr_min.note: This is a DEFINITION, not a pass/fail band: it fixes the level at which comm.effective_range_m reads the crossing (0.50), so the harness's effective range is comparable with published DSRC numbers. The harness curve is proportional-to-PDR (normalised at the near band), so the crossing is an effective range only insofar as the near band is genuinely near-100% delivery.

urban_v2i_max_range_m.cite: urban V2I 802.11p field measurement (max range at FSR > 0.25)
urban_v2i_max_range_m.source: Urban V2I 802.11p measurements report a maximum range of ~700 m, defined as the largest distance at which the frame success ratio stays continuously above 0.25 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/254058759), recorded in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json findings section 4 and listed in docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md as a curve to pin.
urban_v2i_max_range_m.note: READ THE THRESHOLD BEFORE COMPARING: 700 m here is a 25%-frame-success range, NOT a high-PDR range and NOT the 50%-PDR effective range of effective_range_pdr_min. It is roughly the far edge of the gray zone. RSU antennas are also mast-mounted, so a V2I link is far more often LOS than a V2V link at the same distance.

los_high_pdr_range_m.cite: Bai/Stancil/Krishnan MobiCom 2010; Sensors 2021 urban V2I benchmark
los_high_pdr_range_m.source: IEEE 802.11p / DSRC line-of-sight open-road measurements sustain high PDR out to ~500-700 m at ~20 dBm (GM campaigns, Bai/Stancil/Krishnan MobiCom 2010; urban V2I benchmark, Sensors 2021, PMC8347901). Summarised in research-realism-benchmarks.json benchmarks[10] (V2X PDR-vs-distance reference points).
los_high_pdr_range_m.derivation: An interval assembled from two campaigns with different success criteria, hence coarse rather than anchored.
los_high_pdr_range_m.note: CAVEAT ADDED 2026-08-30 -- the 700 m upper edge collides with urban_v2i_max_range_m, where 700 m is measured at a frame success ratio of only 0.25. Treat 500 m as the defensible high-PDR LOS anchor and 700 m as the outer edge reachable at low success ratio; do not quote '700 m at high PDR'. Consistency check with the pinned constants: TR 37.885 highway LOS at 500 m needs 20.8 dBm EIRP against a -81 dBm receiver, which matches the '~20 dBm' quoted for those campaigns.

nlos_urban_effective_range_m.source: Urban NLoS reception collapses to an effective range 'on the order of only ~100 m at obstructed intersections' (research-realism-benchmarks.json benchmarks[10], V2X PDR-vs-distance reference points).
nlos_urban_effective_range_m.note: Order-of-magnitude anchor only; no precision beyond one significant figure is claimed. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: TR 37.885 urban NLOS at the ETSI ceiling of 33 dBm EIRP against a -81 dBm receiver closes at 121.9 m (pathloss_37885.nlos_link_budget_consequence_m) -- the standard's formula and this measured anchor agree to well within the one significant figure claimed.

pdr_vs_rssi_curve.cite: FLOURISH Bristol ITS-G5 dataset -- RECIPE WITHDRAWN, see blocking_caveats
pdr_vs_rssi_curve.source: docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md requires 'PDR-vs-RSSI empirical curve, FLOURISH Bristol ITS-G5 (DOI 10.5523/bris.eupowp7h3jl525yxhm3521f57)'. The dataset -- 4 RSUs on a 5 km central-Bristol track, 2 OBUs, 8 sessions of ~2 h, CAMs every 10 ms at 25 dBm and 29 dBm, described in Tassi, Mavromatis & Piechocki, 'A dataset of full-stack ITS-G5 DSRC communications over licensed and unlicensed bands using a large-scale urban testbed', Data in Brief 25:104368, 2019, doi:10.1016/j.dib.2019.104368 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6727192/, arXiv:1903.10289) -- is NOT vendored in this repository, and no numeric points from it appear in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json or research-realism-benchmarks.json.

blocking_caveats.authors_exclude_this_use: THE DATASET'S OWN AUTHORS RULE OUT THE USE THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN FOR. Verbatim from the Data in Brief abstract: 'The dataset is not intended to be used for signal propagation modelling.' The earlier wording of this entry quoted only the paper's 'suitable for calibrating physical layers of vehicular simulators' and omitted the exclusion sitting beside it. Recorded here on 2026-09-07 after re-reading the source.
blocking_caveats.geometry_mismatch: V2I, NOT V2V. The four RSUs are mast-mounted at roughly 5 m (HW), 8 m (MVB), 12 m (DH) and 25 m (SU); every link in the dataset therefore has one endpoint 3-17x higher than the 1.5 m V2X_ANTENNA_HEIGHT_M this project models. Under the TR 37.885 NLOSv branch rule an antenna at >= 5 m clears every blocker in TR37885_BLOCKER_HEIGHT_M, so these links sit in the 'Case 1 / Case 3' regime while our V2V links sit in 'Case 2'. A PDR-vs-RSSI curve binned from this dataset is a curve for a DIFFERENT link population.
blocking_caveats.licence: THE PAPER AND THE DATASET CARRY DIFFERENT LICENCES. The Data in Brief article is CC BY 4.0; the DATASET at doi:10.5523/bris.eupowp7h3jl525yxhm3521f57 is released under the Non-Commercial Government Licence for public sector information v2.0 -- open to read, NON-COMMERCIAL only. Under the project rule 'data whose licence is not clearly stated is never committed, and neither are numbers derived from it', the licence here IS clearly stated but is non-commercial, so any derived numbers must be cached in a gitignored path and the restriction carried with them. Both licences verified first-hand on 2026-09-07.

pdr_vs_rssi_curve.note: PLACEHOLDER, deliberately empty, AND THE RECIPE THAT USED TO SIT HERE IS WITHDRAWN. Do not 'download the dataset, bin MAC-layer delivery by RSSI and pin the points': the authors exclude propagation modelling, the geometry is V2I at 5-25 m against our 1.5 m V2V, and the dataset licence is non-commercial. See blocking_caveats. This remains the named calibration target for nakagami_fading.sinr_to_per_mapping (also unavailable), but closing that gap needs a V2V measurement set at comparable antenna heights whose licence permits the derived numbers to be committed -- not this one.

cv2x_mode4_pdr95_range_m.source: C-V2X Mode 4 simulation benchmark: PDR >= 95% out to 380/300/280 m at densities 0.1/0.2/0.3 veh/m (MCS 9, keep-probability 0.8), doi:10.1007/978-3-031-21967-2_45. Summarised in research-realism-benchmarks.json benchmarks[11] (C-V2X Mode 4).
cv2x_mode4_pdr95_range_m.note: PINNED FOR REFERENCE. This project's stacks model ITS-G5/802.11p, not C-V2X; the entry exists so a future C-V2X profile is graded against an audited number.

latency_p50_ms_80211p.cite: DLR Cohda MK5 field measurements (ITS World Congress 2021)
latency_p50_ms_80211p.source: de Ponte Mueller et al., 'ITS-G5 and C-V2X link level performance measurements', ITS World Congress 2021, https://elib.dlr.de/142341/ : ITS-G5/802.11p minimum end-to-end latency ~5 ms at 200 B payload rising to 8-9 ms at 800/1000 B. Summarised in research-realism-benchmarks.json benchmarks[12] (latency CDF anchors).
latency_p50_ms_80211p.note: PINNED FOR LATER PHASES. Phase 0 datasets carry detection_time == generation_time (no latency model), so no latency metric is scored. Sanity: the 802.11p PPDU airtime alone is 0.312 ms at 200 B and 1.112 ms at 800 B (phy_80211p.frame_airtime_us), so the measured 5-9 ms is dominated by stack/queueing, not by the air interface.

latency_p50_ms_cv2x.cite: DLR Cohda MK6c field measurements (ITS World Congress 2021)
latency_p50_ms_cv2x.source: Same DLR Cohda MK5/MK6c field campaign as latency_p50_ms_80211p (de Ponte Mueller et al., ITS World Congress 2021, https://elib.dlr.de/142341/): C-V2X (LTE PC5 mode 4, SPS) end-to-end latency ~25 ms typical, rising to 40-45 ms (1-sigma) for 800-1000 B packets.
latency_p50_ms_cv2x.note: PINNED FOR REFERENCE; not scored in Phase 0.

shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m.cite: ETSI TR 103 257-1 / Gudmundson correlation model (ROADMAP section 3.2)
shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m.source: Gudmundson-style AR(1) shadowing with a 10-13 m decorrelation distance, adopted in docs/realism/ROADMAP.md section 3.2 item 3 and gated in the Phase-2 benchmark list as 'empirical link-level autocorrelation e-folding distance 10 +/- 3 m (ETSI TR 103 257-1)'. ETSI TR 103 257-1 V1.1.1 (2019), 'Analysis of V2X radio channel models', https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_tr/103200_103299/10325701/01.01.01_60/tr_10325701v010101p.pdf , specifies an urban model with correlated log-normal shadowing of sigma = 3 dB and a 10 m decorrelation distance.
shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m.derivation: Range [7, 13] m is the ROADMAP's '10 +/- 3 m' gate written out as an interval.
shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m.note: PINNED FOR PHASE 2 (channel model); no shadowing autocorrelation is observable in the Phase-0 dataset schema. THIS IS THE GATE; the per-state MODEL INPUTS are pathloss_37885.shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m (10 m LOS, 13 m NLOSv/NLOS, both inside this interval). NOT VALIDATED, AND EVERY MEASUREMENT FOUND SO FAR FALLS OUTSIDE IT -- IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Urban measurements are SHORTER: 4.25 m LOS / 4.5 m OLOS on ordinary urban streets (pathloss_37885.measured_decorrelation_is_environment_dependent, Abbas et al. 2015, CC BY 3.0) and 2.2-3.7 m median at two Gothenburg intersections (pathloss_37885.intersection_measured_decorrelation_distance_m, Nilsson et al. 2018, CC BY 4.0). Highway measurements are LONGER: 23.3 m LOS / 32.5 m OLOS. This interval is a Gudmundson/ETSI open-street modelling convention, not a measured envelope; it is retained UNCHANGED as the Phase-2 gate so the conformance test keeps grading the model we chose to implement, and the disagreement is recorded rather than tuned away. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT (restated 2026-09-07 after a withdrawal): the ABSOLUTE urban comparison carries a confound -- Nilsson et al. reach 2-4 m only 'in cases where a proper model for the path loss AND THE ANTENNA PATTERN is included' and say that 'otherwise, the de-correlation distance has to be much longer', and our channel has NO antenna-pattern term (pathloss_37885.no_antenna_gain_or_pattern_term), so this gate is NOT falsified by those numbers. What IS established, confound-free, is the ENVIRONMENT RATIO: Abbas et al. measure urban and highway in one campaign under identical processing and find highway 5.48x (LOS) to 7.22x (OLOS) longer than urban, which no single constant can express. See docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 2 and its section 0 item W2.
